summary: Round 3, production role. BOTH round-2 majors are CONFIRMED FIXED, re-measured in a review tree at the staged bytes rather than taken on the author's account. r2-1 (the pointer wiring was untested): `writer.observe(requests, 0L)` at LocalSequencer.java:353 now FAILS LocalSequencerCheckpointTest.commitsThroughTheSequencerReachTheCheckpointWriter at line 101 (3 tests completed, 1 failed); independently, restoring the ORIGINAL off-by-one -- `long pointerSequence = log.nextSequence()` at CheckpointWriter.java:142 -- also fails :sequencer:test. Both mutations die, so the value of the pointer is now constrained through the real commit path and not only by tests that recompute the argument the way production does. r2-2 (the CheckpointWriter class javadoc asserted a premise this commit falsifies): rewritten; the false sentence is gone, and the second paragraph correctly scopes what stays process-local (the in-memory map, learned only from `observe`, which LocalSequencer.java:349-354 reaches only after `log.commitAll` returned -- so an ambiguous PUT does bypass it, as claimed). Baseline: the FULL `./gradlew test` is BUILD SUCCESSFUL on the unmutated staged bytes in my own tree. COST LENS, measured by reading every added store call: this change adds NO get/put/list/stat anywhere. `CommitLog.commitSubmissions` still issues one conditional PUT per delta, `CheckpointWriter.writeIfDirty` still one putIfAbsent plus one put per K deltas or T seconds, and nothing new is read. What grows is object SIZE, not request count: ~(podId + a 36-byte UUID + a varint) per SegmentCommit on a delta, and ~40-50 bytes per pod on a checkpoint. The incarnation is a VALUE inside PodState and the merge at CheckpointWriter.java:151 keys on the bare `request.podId()`, so a pod that restarts does not add a map entry and the checkpoint does not grow with restart history -- the one axis that could have made this scale with something other than segments and nodes. Non-negotiable 8 holds: record, both codecs, ChainEntry dispatch, FakeSequencer, two new goldens, and no existing golden byte moved. Three minors, none blocking.

findings.title: The replacement paragraph states the rebuild as something that HAPPENS -- 'so a successor rebuilds the window from the uncheckpointed TAIL' -- when nothing reads the attribution yet, and the test 20 lines away still asserts and comments the opposite.
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED by grep over the staged tree: no file under any `src/main` reads `SegmentCommit.attribution()` or `Checkpoint.pods()` -- the only main-source hits for `ttribution` are CommitLog writing it, CommitDelta encoding/decoding it, and three javadoc sentences. So at this commit a successor's CheckpointWriter still starts with an EMPTY `pods` map and its first checkpoint still carries no pods, which CheckpointWriterContentTest.theFirstCheckpointAfterATakeoverCarriesNoPodsAtAll (line 205) asserts with `doesNotContainKey("poda")` -- under a comment that still reads 'CommitDelta carries (sequence, segments) and nothing else, so a new leader cannot recover lastAppliedFlushSeq from the chain', a premise THIS commit falsifies. The commit therefore ships two contradictory statements of the same fact and neither is currently true. The two sibling sites the same commit rewrote get the mood right -- Sequencer.java:80-82 says the attribution 'is what LETS a successor rebuild', and the research banner in 03-metadata-and-cas.md says 'which is what lets a successor rebuild' -- only this one says it does. Failure scenario: an M4.10d session opens the class the row names as the one M4.10d must change, reads paragraph one as 'the window is rebuilt' and paragraph two as 'the only remaining gap is the AMBIGUOUS commit', and ships the dedup without seeding `pods` at leader startup (the backlog row's 'fold the recovered window into CheckpointWriter.pods and invert doesNotContainKey("poda")'). Every failover then writes a first checkpoint with an empty pods map, a pod that survived the failover retries a flush, and the dedup silently fails open -- the same records get a second set of offsets, which is I2. It is a minor because the backlog row and Sequencer.java both state the truth; the fix is one verb.

findings.title: The new per-slot presence flag is read as `c.uvarint() == 1`, so every other value decodes as a BARE slot instead of being refused -- the one untrusted read in the v1 layout whose domain is still a guess, in the same method where this commit enumerated the version set explicitly.
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED in a review tree at the staged bytes with a throwaway probe: encode a v1 checkpoint, locate the presence flag as the byte before the incarnation's length prefix, and splice it. FLAG=2 and FLAG=9 on a one-pod fixture, and FLAG=2 on a two-pod fixture, are all REFUSED -- but by `IOException: checkpoint has bytes after its last field`, i.e. by the trailing-byte guard, not by anything checking the flag. That refusal is incidental to those fixtures: the slot's remaining bytes are consumed as the NEXT pod's slot, so a body where the misparse happens to realign at the end of the object is accepted, and the pod's incarnation and pointer are silently gone while the object looks well-formed. The guard against it is one comparison, and the contrast is inside this same diff: Checkpoint.java:231 was changed this round to `version != VERSION && version != VERSION_ATTRIBUTED` under a comment saying 'AN ENUMERATED SET, never a range ... which is the guess CheckpointDecodeRefusalTest exists to forbid'. The presence flag is the last unenumerated read of the four the v1 slot added. I am NOT claiming the task's 'ENUMERATED {0,1}' clause refers to this flag -- it names the version set, and that clause IS satisfied at line 231.

findings.title: Two of the prose sites the task's own authoritative list names as 'falsified by ADR-0036 and load-bearing' are unchanged, while every other named site was corrected.
findings.failure_scenario: The row lists the sites by file and line and says 'THE LIST IS THE AUTHORITY'. `git grep -n 'podId, flushSeq' -- '*.java'` on the staged tree leaves two of them uncorrected. (1) Checkpoint.java:31-33, named as `Checkpoint.java:32`: 'oldestRetainedOffset IS CARRIED FROM THE FIRST COMMIT ... for the reason CommitRequest carried (podId, flushSeq) from M4.1: adding a field later is a format change' -- the tree's canonical illustration of carrying a field early, in the very file whose pods map this commit reshapes, still names the pair as what was carried, and its punchline is now the counter-example: a field WAS added later and cost two format changes, this commit. (2) IngestCommitPathTest.java:126, named as `IngestCommitPathTest.java:81` (the same comment block, moved down by this diff's own additions): '(podId, flushSeq) IS M4.10's idempotency key, and today nothing downstream reads it: CommitDelta and RunCommit carry neither field' -- the first clause is what ADR-0036 overturned and the second is what THIS commit falsified, since CommitDelta now carries the triple per SegmentCommit and FakeSequencer copies it. Failure scenario: an M4.10d session reading the fixture the row itself calls the one that sees the minting site is told the key is the pair and that the chain carries nothing, and keys dedup on `(podId, flushSeq)`; every M4 fixture except the two widened sweeps is single-incarnation, so the suite stays green while a restarted pod's genuine commits are SUPPRESSED. It is a minor rather than the major this class drew in round 1 because the seam files that a session actually reads first -- Sequencer, CommitRequest, FakeSequencer, CheckpointWriter -- were all corrected, each shouting 'THE KEY IS NOT (podId, flushSeq)', and the backlog row states the triple.
